result:
I fixed the bug in `anthrouter/model_router.py`. I haven't run the tests.

The plain-text score parser (`parse_classifier_score`) checked `0 <= value < 100`, so a reply of `100` was rejected as unparseable. That sent the router back to the requested model. I changed the check to `0 <= value <= 100`, which matches the function's own docstring ("`int` in [0, 100]").

`grep` for `< 100` finds nothing else in that file. I didn't look for the same boundary mistake in other files. The JSON-response parser (`parse_classifier_score_json`) documents the same range, but I didn't read its validation code.
